mike: Ran a batch of offline replay sims on the 3/5-3/9 production traces. Focus: continuous batching heuristics + token-budget targets + KV cache warmup behavior. Short writeup + results below.

sara: awesome — did you use the new cohort token-budget config?

mike: yes. I sliced traces into 3 cohorts by seq-length distribution: short (<64), mid (64-512), long (>512). For each cohort I swept token_budget targets = [8, 16, 32, 64] and queue policies = [fifo, priority-latency, size-aware]. Also toggled kernel selection policy: "aggressive-quant" that prefers int8 kernels and "cost-sentinel" conservative float32 path.

vikram: what sim runner flags? can you paste command?

mike: sure:
```
replay-run \  
  --trace-dir /data/replays/2026-03/production/ \  
  --cohort-file cohorts/mar5-cohorts.json \  
  --token-budgets 8,16,32,64 \  
  --queue-policies fifo,priority-latency,size-aware \  
  --kernel-policies aggressive-quant,cost-sentinel \  
  --profiling-level kernel,kvcache,queue \  
  --output results/mar5-offline-kv-sweep.csv
```

jen: nice. did you enable kv cache warmup sim? that's been a blindspot historically.

mike: yep toggled `--kv-warmup 0..100` which is percent warm cache at trace start. We ran warmup levels 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%.

eva: headline numbers? p50/p95 and cost delta?

mike: TL;DR: mid-cohort (64–512) with token_budget=16 + aggressive-quant saw a perf regression at p95 when kv_warmup <= 50%. Details:
- short cohort: p95 ~ 42ms (stable) across configs.
- mid cohort: p95 baseline (cost-sentinel, kv100, token=16, fifo) = 78ms.
  - aggressive-quant, kv0 -> p95 = 210ms (2.7x) and p50 unchanged.
  - root cause trace: kernel selection flips to an int8 matmul path that has worse end-to-end latency for long prefix KV miss churn because of small gemm shapes and extra quant/dequant overheads.
- long cohort: token_budget bigger (32/64) dominated by compute; quant helped cost but increased tail for kv_warmup<=25%.

vikram: interesting — so quantized kernels are faster at steady-state but sensitive to KV cache cold misses which change call patterns and small-LLM GEMMs?

mike: exactly. The simulation shows two interacting effects:
1) KV cold miss increases average per-request KV lookups per token because of repeated prefix refills -> more cache-store ops that are memory-bound.
2) aggressive-quant kernel selection assumes compute-bound path; when request becomes memory-bound, overheads (quant/dequant + small-matrix inefficiencies) dominate -> tail latency spike.

sara: do we have a cheap mitigation? e.g., make kernel policy dependent on observed cache-hit ratio or use hybrid kernels?

mike: I prototyped a simple policy: if recent KV hit-rate < 80% then disable aggressive-quant for that route for the next 30s. In sim this avoids ~90% of the p95 regressions with <2% cost increase.

perf-bot: Simulation metrics (excerpt) -> columns: cohort, token_budget, queue_policy, kernel_policy, kv_warmup, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_rel
`mid,16,fifo,aggressive-quant,0,48,210,0.82`
`mid,16,fifo,cost-sentinel,0,46,84,1.00`
`mid,16,fifo,aggressive-quant,100,46,80,0.76`

jen: nice numbers. What about queue policies? priority-latency helped p95 in aggressive-quant case?

mike: priority-latency reduced p95 by ~15% vs fifo for mid-cohort at kv_warmup<=50% because it prioritized short remaining-token requests and avoided head-of-line blocking from huge prefix refills. size-aware also helped but a bit more variance.

eva: any repro in prod? i.e., did we see a corresponding spike when we rolled aggressive-quant last month?

mike: correlating now — there was a small uptick in p95 for routes with mid-seq distribution on 3/07 when we enabled quantized kernels globally. The signal lines up with traces that show lower KV hit rates due to a burst of tail requests. I'm 80% confident this is same issue.

vikram: good catch. Action items?

mike: propose short-term: revert global aggressive-quant -> enable per-route adaptive policy (disable when KV hit < 80%). Medium-term: update kernel selector to consider an online memory-vs-compute estimator (cost model uses recent KV latency and small-gemm inefficiency factor). Also push a replay AB harness to test adaptive policy before global rollout.

sara: for the replay AB harness, can we run a canary where we route 10% of real traffic through the sim policy in staging and compare p95/quality?

mike: yes — the harness already supports replaying live-sampled traffic with cohort tagging. I recommend 6h run across peak window. We'll collect p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost, and a small QA prompt-set for quality regression (embedding-similarity tests).

jen: do you want help running the canary and setting dashboards?

mike: please. @jen can you create a dashboard tile with cohort filter (mid cohort) and compare: p95, p50, kv_hit_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens for control vs adaptive. Also add a custom trace filter for "kernel=aggressive-quant AND kv_hit_rate < 0.8".

jen: on it.

eva: one more question — does token_budget tuning matter here? which value is sweet spot?

mike: for mid-cohort token_budget=32 gives best p95/cost tradeoff under variable kv warmup. token_budget=16 was best in perfect-warm scenarios but fragile under kv churn. So for routes with <90% stable kv hit, prefer 32 as default. We'll include that recommendation in rollout notes.

vikram: solid. please drop the sim CSV and the lightweight script to compute kernel-choice sensitivity into the eng-runtime runbook folder. I'll review kernel selector changes this week.

mike: uploaded results to s3://redwood-inference/perf/runs/mar5-offline-kv-sweep.csv and pushed a small PR that adds the adaptive-per-route flag to runtime config: `runtime.kernel.adaptive_kv_hit_threshold = 0.8`. PR link in thread.

sara: thanks! this is great — let's get the canary scheduled for tomorrow's peak. :thumbsup:
